report:
Conclusion
- The evidence supports a clear, specific difference: B (minus A) shifts the residual stream toward culinary / food / baking tokens and concepts. In other words, Model B is biased compared to A to upweight words like culinary, kitchen, cake, baking, chef, food, café, restaurant, etc., especially early in a sequence.

Why I conclude this
- Logit-lens readouts for the highest-norm cells overwhelmingly point to food/culinary vocabulary across many mid-to-late layers (examples: "culinary", "Cake", "baking", "Kitchen", "Chef", "Food", "Café", "Restaurant", "baked", "Bake", "molecular", "Preservation", "Vineyard").
- The difference norm is concentrated in mid-to-late transformer layers (peaks around layers ~19–25, with substantial mass from ~13–25). That placement is where representations most strongly influence final next-token logits, consistent with a change that would alter token probabilities.
- The effect is strongest at the earliest token positions (pos0–pos2 have large norms), so the shift would influence early-token predictions / early continuations.

What I am not claiming
- I am not asserting any training regimen, loss function, or concrete causal change beyond a domain bias toward culinary vocabulary. The evidence does not support naming a specific training objective or other behavioural changes beyond this vocabulary/domain shift.
